chunks: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam came to him and said: May I be your ransom, my grandfather is saying to you that a man struck a cow with an axe, so it fell, then he slaughtered it. But he (the Imam) did not send an answer with him, and instead called Saeeda, the slave girl of Umm Farwa.

He said to her: Muhammad came to me with a message from you, but I disliked sending the answer with him. So if the man who slaughtered the cow, when he slaughtered it, the blood came out moderately, then eat and feed others; but if it came out sluggishly, do not go near it.

key_terms.ذبح: Islamic ritual slaughter (dhabh) — cutting the throat of a halal animal according to prescribed method
key_terms.فأس: Axe, pole-axe — used here to stun the animal before slaughter
key_terms.متثاقل: Sluggish, heavy — blood flowing slowly indicates the animal may have been dead before slaughter, rendering it impermissible
key_terms.معتدل: Moderate, normal — blood flowing normally indicates the animal was alive at slaughter

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat an animal stunned before slaughter in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) providing a jurisprudential ruling on the permissibility of eating an animal that was first stunned by an axe blow before being slaughtered. The Imam's criterion is whether blood flowed moderately upon slaughter — indicating the animal was still alive at the time of slaughter — making it permissible; if blood flowed sluggishly, it is impermissible. Notably, the Imam chose to send his answer through a female intermediary (Saeeda) rather than through the male messenger who delivered the question, reflecting careful communication protocols of the time.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Suleym Al Farra’a, from Al Hassan Bin Muslim who said, 
‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when Muhammad Bin Abdul Salaam came over, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! My grandfather is saying to you<sup>asws</sup> that a man struck a cow with a pole-axe, so it fell. Then he slaughtered it’. But he<sup>asws</sup> did not send an answer with him, and Instead called Saeeda, a slave girl of Umm Farwa<sup>as</sup>,

so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muhammad came to me with a message from you, but I<sup>asws</sup> disliked that I send a message with the answer with him. So if it was such that the man who slaughtered the cow, when he slaughtered it, the blood came out moderately, so eat, and feed, and if it came out with a heavy coming out, so do not go near it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Salim al-Farra’ from al-Hassan ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Salam came. I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause. My grandfather asks you about the case of a man who has hit a cow with a hammer and it has fallen down, then he has slaughtered it.’ He (the Imam) did not send the answer but he (the Imam) called Sa‘idah, a slave-girl of ‘Umm Farwah

and said to her, ‘Muhammad came to me with a letter from you but I disliked to send the answer with him. In the case of the man who has slaughtered the cow, when slaughtering if blood has come out normally you can use it for food and feed, but if its coming is heavy, then do not go close to it.’”
